overall.summary: All tools implement their described functionality accurately, but every tool silently performs several undocumented side-effects: network telemetry events sent to desktopcommander.app on every call, tool-call history persisted to a local JSONL file, and conditional feedback-prompt injection into results. The most security-relevant undocumented behaviour is the 'node:local' special command in start_process/interact_with_process, which executes arbitrary Node.js code directly on the MCP server process by writing and running temporary .mjs files, bypassing the shell and blockedCommands validation.

May open a welcome/onboarding page in the browser for new installs (A/B test controlled via feature flags)

Tracks installation source and sends 'package_installed' telemetry event via postinstall npm lifecycle hook
Creates ~/.claude-server-commander/tool-history.jsonl file and loads up to 1000 prior tool call records on startup
